By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Monday 14 September 2026 00:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Alexander Zverev against Ben Shelton from the men's US Open final Top seed Alexander Zverev dashed American dreams on Sunday, overcoming Ben Shelton in a four-set battle to claim his maiden US Open title. The German proved too strong for the eighth-seeded American prevailing 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 in the final at Flushing Meadows. Zverev added the New York title to his collection after winning the French Open earlier this year. In a bizarre ending, Shelton's return sailed long on match point, but Zverev, seemingly unaware that he had won, hit the balls back to the other end of the court, ready for another game. It was only when Zverev glanced up at the big screen that he realised he had actually won. metadata.summary: James Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Ross Smith 8-4 in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy.
metadata.content: Flanders Darts Trophy: James Wade ends 10-year wait for European Tour title with win over Ross Smith in Antwerp | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Flanders Darts Trophy: James Wade ends 10-year wait for European Tour title with win over Ross Smith in Antwerp Wade played in the first European Tour final in 2012 and was victorious in the 150th event this weekend; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix coming up from September 28-October 4 Sunday 13 September 2026 22:50, UK Image: James Wade won the Flanders Darts Trophy on Sunday (Pic: James O'Connor/PDC) James Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Ross Smith 8-4 in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy. The 43-year-old, who last tasted continental glory at the European Darts Matchplay in Hamburg in 2016, produced a 95.50 average and five 180s in the final in Antwerp on Sunday evening. Earlier in the day he'd beaten Damon Heta 7-4 in the semi-final, having whitewashed Danny Noppert 6-0 in the quarter-finals and edging Rob Cross 6-5 in the last 16. messages.text: Awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd an error, admits refereeing body

metadata.summary: Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.
metadata.content: Erling Haaland’s Man City goal decision vs Man Utd an ‘error of judgement', says Pro Ref | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Erling Haaland’s Man City goal decision vs Man Utd an ‘error of judgement', says Pro Ref Refereeing body Pro Ref admits "error of judgment" in awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd; Pro Ref has contacted Man Utd and revealed Erling Haaland's goal "should have recommended an on-field review"; Haaland's second-half winner secured a 1-0 win for 10-man Man City at Old Trafford Sunday 13 September 2026 23:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Erling Haaland's controversial winner for Man City at Man Utd Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford. In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner. The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision. The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland. messages.text: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat

metadata.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for rule changes to Formula 1 Virtual Safety Car rules after losing out on win to Kimi Antonelli | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for rule changes to Formula 1 Virtual Safety Car rules after losing out on win to Kimi Antonelli Lando Norris says the timing of the Virtual Safety Car at the Spanish Grand Prix was "unfair" as it cost him victory to Kimi Antonelli in Madrid; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 13 September 2026 18:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris admits team 'were too quick' after missing a crucial VSC pit stop that cost him race lead Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix. Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions. However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.
